scenarios.title: A Question About {Pf}
text: At {SET}, {JR} from {OUT} slips in a question that has nothing to do with football: 'Your relationship with {P} is all over social media. Is she a distraction?'
The last question at {SET} comes from a tabloid reporter at the back: 'Is it true {P} has been seen at training more often? Does the coach mind?'
scenarios.prompt: How do you answer a question about your partner?

choices.label: 'She's the reason I'm playing well.'
choices.hint: {Pf} reacts depending on how private she is.
choices.text: The quote becomes a headline. Fans call it romantic. Whether {Pf} loves it or hates it depends entirely on who she is.

choices.label: 'My private life is private.'
choices.text: Said politely, without a smile. The room moves on. {Pf} hears about it and sends a heart emoji.

choices.label: Make a joke at her expense
choices.hint: The room laughs. She might not.
choices.text: The reporters laugh. The clip is everywhere by dinner. {Pf} watches it twice and doesn't reply to his messages until morning.

scenarios.title: The Blame Question
text: After the result, {JR} asks directly: 'Was {T}'s mistake the reason you didn't win?' Every camera in the room swings to {J}.
At {SET}, a reporter replays the moment {T} lost the ball for the goal, then asks {J} what he said to him in the dressing room.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate is being blamed in public.

choices.label: Defend him completely
choices.text: 'We win together, we lose together. Next question.' {T} reads the quote on his phone in the canteen and looks over at {J} for a long moment.

choices.label: Be honest: 'It cost us.'
choices.text: 'It was a mistake and it cost us.' True. Also the back page. {T} doesn't speak to him for a week.

choices.label: Blame yourself instead
choices.hint: Noble. The media will run with it.
choices.text: 'I should have tracked my runner. That's on me.' It isn't, really. {T} knows it. {CAPl} knows it.

scenarios.title: The Ownership Question
text: At {SET}, {JR} asks about the club's finances: 'Do the players trust President {PRES}'s plan?' The club's press officer stiffens.
A reporter asks: 'Fans say the board has no ambition. Do you agree?' The press officer reaches for the microphone, then stops.

choices.label: Back the board
choices.hint: Board grateful. Fans roll their eyes.
choices.text: 'We trust the president and the project.' {PRESl} sends a thank-you message. The fan forums are less grateful.

choices.label: Side with the fans
choices.hint: Fans love it. The board will remember.
choices.text: 'The fans deserve ambition, and so do we.' The ultras put the quote on a flag. A director calls his agent.

choices.label: 'That's above my pay grade.'
choices.text: The room laughs. The press officer exhales. Nobody's happy, nobody's angry.

scenarios.title: The Family Story
text: A TV interviewer wants to talk about {J}'s childhood: the poverty, the bus fares, {DAD}'s job. She has clearly spoken to someone from his neighbourhood. She has details.
{OUT} wants to run a big feature on 'the sacrifices of {J}'s family'. They want quotes from {J}. And photos of the old house.

out.text: The story is beautiful. People cry. {MUM} prints it out. {DAD} says only, 'You made us sound better than we were.' He sounds pleased.
The story is beautiful, but it shows the old house and names the street. {DAD} is ashamed. He doesn't call for two weeks.

choices.label: Ask your parents first
choices.text: {DAD} says no photos. {MUM} says yes to everything. They compromise. The piece is gentler and truer for it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines. {JR} writes it anyway, from other sources, and gets half of it wrong.

scenarios.title: 'Is There a Problem With the Coach?'
text: {JR}: 'You've been dropped three times this month. Sources say you and {Mf} don't speak. Is there a problem?' Silence. The press officer's pen stops.
At {SET}, a reporter reads out a fan's question: 'Why does the coach hate {J}?' The room laughs nervously.
scenarios.prompt: Your relationship with the manager, in public.

choices.label: 'I respect him. I'll earn my place.'
choices.text: Calm and humble. {Mf} reads it and, the next day, asks him to stay after training for some extra work.

choices.label: 'Ask him.'
choices.text: 'Ask him.' It's the only headline in the country the next morning. {Mf} answers in his own press conference. It's not pretty.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.desc: 'He loves me, he just hides it.'
choices.text: The room laughs. The clip is cute. Nothing is resolved.

scenarios.title: The Family Photo Post
text: {J} took a photo of {MUM} and {DAD} at their kitchen table, laughing at something he said. It's the most real photo he's ever taken. He wants to post it.
{SIB} sends him a photo from home: the whole family in matching shirts with his number. It's ridiculous. It's perfect.

choices.label: Post it with a long caption
choices.hint: The internet melts. Family feels seen.
choices.text: Two million likes. {MUM} reads every comment, all of them, over three days. {DAD} pretends he hasn't seen it.

choices.label: Keep it private
choices.text: He sets it as his phone wallpaper. Nobody else needs to see it.

choices.label: Post it, but crop out {DAD}
choices.text: {DAD} notices immediately. 'Good, I hate photos,' he says. He's quiet for a while.

scenarios.title: Beef With a Rival Player
text: A player from {R} posts a video mocking {J}'s celebration. It has a million views. The comments are full of {J}'s own fans asking him to respond.
A rival defender posts: 'Some players are all TikTok and no tackles.' He doesn't tag {J}. He doesn't need to.

choices.label: Clap back with a joke
choices.hint: Fans love it. Rivalry heats up.
choices.text: His reply is so good that even the rival's teammates like it. The next derby is the most-anticipated match of the season.

choices.label: Answer on the pitch
choices.text: He says nothing. Fans make 'answer on the pitch' a hashtag. The pressure is enormous.

choices.label: Message him privately
choices.text: A private message: 'Good video. See you Sunday.' The rival replies with a laughing emoji. Respect, of a sort.

scenarios.title: The Documentary
text: A streaming service is filming a documentary about the club. They want {J} as one of the main characters: cameras at training, at home, in the car.
The documentary producers want to film {J}'s family back home. They say it will be 'the emotional heart of the series'.

choices.label: Full access
choices.hint: Global fame. Zero privacy. Family feelings.
choices.text: The series is a hit. {J} becomes famous in countries he's never visited. {MUM} becomes famous too, and hates it a little.

choices.label: Football only
choices.text: He keeps the cameras on the pitch. He's in it enough to be noticed, not enough to be consumed by it.

choices.label: No
choices.text: He declines. He's in the background of one scene, looking annoyed at a camera. It becomes a meme.

scenarios.title: The Tabloid Calls {MUM}
text: A tabloid journalist has turned up at {MUM}'s door pretending to be a family friend. She talked for an hour before realising. Now they have quotes.
A reporter has been calling relatives, asking about an uncle who went to prison twenty years ago. {DAD} has stopped answering the phone.

choices.label: Go public with your anger
choices.text: His post goes viral. Fans flood the paper's comments. Other outlets take his side. That paper will never write kindly about him again.

choices.label: Lawyers, quietly
choices.text: A lawyer's letter kills the story before it runs. {MUM} never knows how close it came.

ok.text: {JR} makes a few calls. The story is quietly dropped. 'You owe me lunch,' says {JR}.

bad.text: {JR} says he can't interfere with another outlet. The story runs. {MUM} cries.

scenarios.title: Caught Being Kind
text: Someone filmed {J} giving his jacket to a homeless man outside {PLACE} at midnight. He didn't know he was being filmed. Now everyone knows.
A hidden-camera video shows {J} paying for an old woman's groceries. It's been viewed four million times.

choices.label: Say nothing at all
choices.text: He never mentions it. That makes people love it even more.

choices.label: Use it to promote a charity
choices.text: He points everyone to a homeless charity. Donations triple. A few cynics call it a PR stunt. Most people don't.

scenarios.title: Lost in Translation
text: An interview in the local language goes badly: {J} meant to say 'the fans here are passionate', but the translation reads 'the fans here are crazy'. It's the headline.
A foreign outlet has mistranslated {J} saying he 'dreams of playing in a bigger league'. He said he 'dreams of playing in big games'.

choices.label: Video apology in the local language
choices.text: His grammar is terrible, his intent obvious. The fans forgive him instantly and adopt his mistakes as chants.

choices.label: Let the club issue a correction
choices.text: The correction is accurate and nobody reads it.

scenarios.title: The Couple Campaign
text: A clothing brand wants {J} and {P} together for a campaign. Real money. Photos everywhere. Billboards with both their faces.
A jewellery brand offers {J} and {Pf} a joint deal. 'Football's favourite couple', the pitch deck says.

choices.label: Ask {Pf} first
choices.text: He asks. Her answer depends on who she is — but she appreciates being asked, either way.

choices.label: Sign it for both of you
choices.text: He signs. She finds out from the brand's email. Whether it's a gift or a betrayal depends entirely on her.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines. The brand signs another couple. Their billboard is enormous. {J} doesn't mind.

scenarios.title: Comments About {MUM}
text: After a bad game, someone in {J}'s comments writes something vile about his mother. It has 2,000 likes.
A troll account has been posting edited photos of {J}'s family for a week. {SIB} has seen them.

choices.label: Respond furiously
choices.text: His reply is furious and justified and becomes its own story. The club's media team asks him to 'take a breath'. {MUM} asks him to delete it.

choices.label: Report and block, say nothing
choices.text: He reports it, blocks them, and calls {MUM} to check she's okay. She hasn't seen it. He makes sure she never does.

choices.label: Post about online abuse
choices.text: His post about abuse gets picked up by national news. The platform deletes two hundred accounts. It's a start.

scenarios.title: The Rumour Reaches Home
text: A transfer rumour links {J} with a club abroad. It's probably nonsense. {MUM} has read it three times and called him twice, crying, asking if he's leaving.
A rumour says {J} is moving abroad. His family's neighbours are already congratulating them. {DAD} wants to know why he heard it from the neighbours.
scenarios.prompt: The rumour hits home before you.

choices.label: Call them, tell them everything
choices.text: He explains it's just a rumour, and promises they'll hear everything from him first. {DAD} says, 'Good. That's all.'

choices.label: Post a denial publicly
choices.text: 'I'm happy here.' The rumour dies. Fans cheer. His agent, who started the rumour, is quietly furious.

choices.label: Let it run
choices.text: He lets it run. His value goes up. His family's worry does too.

scenarios.title: Live on TV
text: A live post-match TV interview. Adrenaline still pumping. The presenter asks about the referee. {J} feels a word forming that should not be said on live TV.
Live TV, pitchside, rain dripping off his eyebrows. The interviewer asks what he'll say to {R}'s fans.

choices.label: Breathe, say something boring
choices.text: 'We take the positives and look forward to the next game.' The most boring sentence in football. It saves him a fine.

choices.label: Say exactly what you think
choices.hint: Viral. Fines. Legend status for some.
choices.text: He says it. The clip has ten million views by midnight. The league fines him. Half the country thinks he's a hero; the other half thinks he's a disgrace.

choices.label: Make the presenter laugh
choices.text: He makes a joke about the rain. The presenter laughs mid-question. The clip is the most-shared of the weekend for nicer reasons.

scenarios.title: {JR} Needs a Favour
text: {JR} has been fair to {J} for years. Now he needs a favour: an exclusive about a teammate's transfer, before anyone else has it. His editor is threatening to cut his job.
{JR} messages late at night. He's heard a rumour about the manager's future. He needs {J} to confirm or deny. Off the record. Please.
scenarios.prompt: Help your friend in the press?

choices.label: Give him the exclusive
choices.hint: {JR} saved. If the squad finds out...

out.text: {JR} gets his scoop and keeps his job. Nobody traces it back. {JR} will owe {J} forever.
The scoop runs. The dressing room works out the source within a day. {CAPl} looks at {J} like a stranger.

choices.label: Refuse, but help another way
choices.text: 'I can't give you that. But I'll give you an exclusive interview about me.' {JR} takes it. His editor is satisfied.

choices.label: Refuse flatly
choices.text: 'No.' {JR} says he understands. His next piece about {J} is noticeably colder.

scenarios.title: The Award Speech
text: {J} has won a monthly award and has thirty seconds to speak on live TV. He can thank anyone. Everyone he's ever known is watching.
At the league's awards night, {J}'s name is called. He walks up with no speech prepared.

choices.label: {MUM} and {DAD}, by name
choices.text: '{MUM}, {DAD} — this is yours.' Back home, the whole street cheers at the TV. {DAD} goes outside 'for air'.

choices.label: The team and the manager
choices.text: He thanks the squad, {Mf}, the kit man, the chef. The squad sing his name on the bus.

choices.label: {Pf}
choices.text: 'And {Pf}. For everything.' Cameras find her in the crowd. She's crying. So is half the internet.

choices.label: The fans
choices.text: 'This is for the people in the stands every week.' The ultras make it their new banner.

scenarios.title: Photographed at the Hospital
text: {J} visits {DAD} in hospital for a minor operation. A photographer catches him in the corridor looking exhausted. The headline: '{J} Family Health Scare'.
A gossip site posts a photo of {J} at a clinic. They speculate wildly. It was a dentist appointment.

choices.label: Explain calmly
choices.text: A short statement ends the story. {DAD} is mortified to be in the news at all.

choices.label: Condemn the intrusion
choices.text: His statement about privacy is widely shared. Other players back him. Photographers become more careful, for a while.

scenarios.title: The Media Darling
text: The press love {J}. He's quotable, accessible, generous. Every outlet wants him. {OUT} calls him 'the face of the league'.
Journalists fight over interviews with {J}. Even critical columnists write about him kindly.

choices.label: Use it for causes you care about
choices.text: He uses every interview to mention his foundation, his old neighbourhood, a teammate who deserves more credit. The goodwill grows.

choices.label: Become the main character
choices.text: Three interviews a week. His face is everywhere. Some teammates start calling him 'the celebrity'.

choices.label: Step back a little
choices.text: He turns down half the requests. Scarcity makes him more valuable. The press respects it.

scenarios.title: At War With the Press
text: Every outlet is against {J} now. Every misplaced pass is a column. Every quiet game is 'proof'. {OUT} has published three negative pieces this week.
The press has turned. Journalists who used to praise him now write about his 'attitude', his 'lifestyle', his 'decline'.
scenarios.prompt: How do you fight a war with the media?

choices.label: Charm offensive
choices.text: One by one, he sits down with them. Off the record, honest, humble. It takes weeks. Slowly, the tone shifts.

choices.label: Go around them
choices.hint: Fans love it. Press hates it more.
choices.text: He starts a weekly video for fans. No journalists needed. The fans love it. The press calls it 'arrogant'.

choices.label: Let your football answer
choices.hint: Only works if you play well.
choices.text: He stops reading. He trains harder. Whether it works depends on Sundays.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Image in Freefall
text: {J}'s public image has collapsed. Brands are 'reviewing' deals. Parents tell their kids to pick a different favourite player. {OUT} runs a poll: 'Is {J} a bad influence?'
The headlines have turned toxic. {J} is now the example columnists use when they write about 'what's wrong with modern footballers'.

choices.label: Public apology and real change
choices.text: A sincere video, no script. Then months of quiet good behaviour. It takes time. Time is the only thing that works.

choices.label: Embrace the villain role
choices.desc: If they hate you, let them.
choices.hint: Some fans love a villain. Sponsors don't.
choices.text: He leans into it: the sneer, the celebrations, the attitude. Away fans hate him. Some home fans love him more. The board is horrified.

choices.label: Disappear for a while
choices.hint: Out of sight, slowly out of mind.
choices.text: Total silence for a month. The story dies of starvation.

scenarios.title: A National Role Model
text: {J} has become a genuine role model. Schools invite him to speak. Parents name their children after him. A government minister mentions him in a speech about youth sport.
A national survey names {J} the most admired athlete among teenagers. His family's phone hasn't stopped ringing.
scenarios.prompt: What do you do with it?

choices.label: Become an ambassador for a cause
choices.text: He becomes an ambassador for youth sport in poor areas. Pitches get built in his name. That will outlast any goal.

choices.label: Stay humble, say nothing
choices.text: He shrugs it off in interviews. The humility makes people admire him more.

scenarios.title: A Fake Video
text: A video is spreading of {J} saying terrible things about his own fans. It's fake — made with software — but it's convincing. It has three million views.
A doctored clip appears to show {J} mocking a disabled fan. It's fake. The internet doesn't wait for facts.

choices.label: Go live and talk directly
choices.desc: Face to face with your fans.
choices.text: He goes live for twenty minutes, calm and clear. The fans believe him. The fake video becomes a story about fake videos.

choices.label: Let the club's lawyers handle it
choices.text: The takedown requests work eventually. For three days, a lot of people believe it.

scenarios.title: The Fans' Favourite
text: {J} is the most popular player at {club}. His shirt outsells everyone's. The ultras' new banner is twenty metres long and has his face on it.
The fans voted: {J} is their favourite player by a landslide. The club shop has run out of his name letters.
scenarios.prompt: How do you repay that love?

choices.label: Spend a day with the supporters' clubs
choices.text: He visits four supporters' clubs in one day: tea, photos, a karaoke song, a cake. The bond becomes unbreakable.

choices.label: Promise you'll never leave
choices.text: 'I'm never leaving.' The stadium roars. Every transfer window from now on will be complicated.

choices.label: Stay grounded
choices.text: Humble words, a wave. The fans love him more for not making it about himself.

scenarios.title: The Fans Have Turned
text: The boos started quietly. Now they're loud. When {J}'s name is read out before kick-off, a section of the stadium whistles. A banner says '{J} OUT'.
Social media is a war zone. Club forums have threads titled 'Why we must sell {J}'. A fan throws a scarf at him after the final whistle.
scenarios.prompt: How do you win them back?

choices.label: Face them directly
choices.desc: Walk to the stand after the match.

ok.text: He walks to the angry stand and applauds them, hand on heart. The boos fade. Some applaud back. It's a start.

bad.text: He walks to the stand. Something is thrown. Stewards pull him away. The photo is everywhere.

choices.label: Meet the supporters' groups privately
choices.text: Two hours in a supporters' club, mostly listening. Some of what they say is unfair. Some of it isn't. They leave with grudging respect.

choices.label: Ignore them
choices.desc: They'll come round when you score.
choices.text: He blocks it out. The boos continue. Every bad touch is amplified.
